crime_highlights: The appellant was carrying two loaded firearms, both of which had oversized magazines, and a substantial amount of fentanyl when he fled from police
He engaged in a dangerous high-speed car chase before fleeing on foot through a residential neighbourhood
One of the guns discharged when he lost his balance in the backyard of a residence
he stored the guns and the fentanyl in the backyard of another family residence where young children lived
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge carefully considered an enhanced pre-sentence report focusing on the appellant’s family context and the impacts of systemic racism
the sentencing judge concluded that the appellant’s reduced moral culpability as a result of the social context in which he grew up
This finding was open to him on the record and there is no basis to interfere with it.
note: Appeal court upholds finding of reduced culpability; heavily outweighed by aggravating factors

crime_highlights: The appellant entered the couple’s vehicle and put it in drive as the woman struggled to stop him
The woman fell out of the vehicle as the appellant drove away and sustained serious injuries, including facial fractures, a deep head laceration, and a mild traumatic brain injury.
rationale_highlights: To the contrary, the sentencing judge expressly noted that she was taking into account “the obvious applicability of the Gladue features in this case” as a mitigating factor
note: Very short appeal reasons; only one clause states the mitigating effect

crime_highlights: The crime was a serious one involving possession of a loaded altered firearm in a public place.
the appellant was under a prohibition order arising from a prior firearm conviction
rationale_highlights: the sentencing judge took these factors into account and specifically reduced the sentence she would have otherwise imposed on the possession count by one year
We see no error in the sentencing judge’s approach.
note: One-year reduction covers both harsh custody and Morris factors together
